text:
Semantic search over the articles now works in Redis. `python3 /app/search.py < query.json` prints the 5 most similar article IDs, most similar first. I checked it against 51 test queries (random vectors, slightly altered article embeddings and a scaled one) and it matched a separate exact cosine-similarity calculation every time.

**Loading:** The data was clean: 1,000 unique IDs, each with 64 valid, non-zero numbers. Each article is stored in Redis as a record `article:<id>` holding `id`, `title` and its embedding.

**Search index:** I created an index called `idx:articles` using cosine similarity. It compares the query against every article rather than taking shortcuts, so the top 5 are exact. New or changed `article:*` records are added to the index automatically.

**`/app/search.py`:**
- It reads the query from standard input and sends a "nearest 5" search to Redis, which does the similarity work.
- It doesn't read `/data/articles.jsonl` or compute any similarity itself.
- It exits with an error if the query isn't 64 numbers.
- It needs the Python packages `redis` and `numpy`, which are already installed.

**Bug fixed during testing:** My first version printed nothing. The installed Redis Python library (version 8.1) returns search results in a different format by default, which the script didn't read correctly. I now set that format explicitly in the script.

**Persistence:** I saved Redis to disk afterwards, so the articles and the index will survive a Redis restart. Your configuration also saves automatically on its normal schedule.
